column1: # What:  ZAP baseline-scan rule customization for RRMS. Each row tunes a
#        specific ZAP plugin's failure threshold for our context. Two
#        IGNORE categories: (1) Phase-2-deferred security headers we
#        haven't added yet; (2) benign informational ZAP rules that fire
#        on every healthy modern web app and aren't vulnerabilities.
# Why:   `zaproxy/action-baseline@v0.15.0` with `fail_action: true`
#        fails the job on ANY new alert at WARN or FAIL level (zap-
#        baseline.py exit code 1 for FAIL, 2 for WARN). The Plan 2
#        Task 9 red-team run confirmed a clean RRMS app triggers three
#        benign WARN rules (10049 / 10109 / 10112) plus a banner rule
#        (10009) — none are vulnerabilities. Without IGNORE-ing them,
#        every PR (including Plan 2's own) would fail ZAP. Genuinely
#        security-relevant passive rules (missing X-Frame-Options 10020,
#        X-Content-Type-Options 10021, cookie Secure/HttpOnly 10011/
#        10010, info disclosure 10023/10024, etc.) are deliberately left
#        at their default FAIL threshold so a real header/cookie/leak
#        regression still fails the scan. Any NEW IGNORE entry needs a
#        comment justifying why it isn't a vuln.
# Where: Loaded by `.github/workflows/security-zap-pr.yml` and
#        `.github/workflows/security-zap-daily.yml` via the
#        `zaproxy/action-baseline@v0.15.0` action's `rules_file_name`
#        input. Path: `.zap/rules.tsv` (action default).
# When:  Active on every PR open/update (PR workflow) and every weekday
#        02:00 Asia/Taipei (daily workflow).
# Schema: ZAP rule TSV — three tab-separated columns. Sources:
#   https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
#   https://github.com/zaproxy/action-baseline (rules_file_name)
